name: Generalplan Ost
scope: The Nazi SS's planning complex for the settlement and 'Germanization' of occupied Eastern Europe, 1939-1945: the successive drafts of the Generalplan Ost (the Planning Office of Himmler's Reich Commissioner for the Strengthening of Germandom under Konrad Meyer, and the RSHA), the ethnic cleansing, enslavement and mass death of the local populations they provided for, and the Lebensraum thinking behind them. Gerlach (s5) describes it as a number of interconnected plans drawn up by several SS authorities, not one document; Connelly (s4) and Heinemann (s2) treat the drafts, with Wetzel's comments, as the surviving record. It covers the plan's stated aims and the research that served it (s2, s3); it leaves out Nazism's wider ideology except where the plan's own drafts and these sources take it up, and the Holocaust of the Jews except as the plans treat it.

summary: The Generalplan Ost was the SS's set of plans for settling Germans in occupied Eastern Europe up to the Urals. It provided for removing, Germanizing, enslaving or letting die tens of millions of local people judged racially undesirable, to make living space for German and Germanic settlers. It was only partly carried out before Germany's defeat.
notes: Themes searched in the saved sources: world (expansion, war), society (ethnic composition, settlement, race), economy, government, liberty. The plan's surviving record is on settlement, expulsion and mass death, so all other statements are null. The DFG catalogue PDF could not be fetched by any download agent.
